finding.claim: HIGH: dropTable ignores the Authorize result, so any authenticated user can reach the destructive DROP TABLE path. Severity HIGH is the authenticated low-privilege ceiling.
finding.source: Authenticated request to POST /admin/drop from any user whose context user passes upstream auth (no dba role required)

trace.note: userFrom reads context value "user" with an unchecked type assertion
Authorize(u, "dba") called; the returned forbidden error is discarded
runSQL executes regardless of authorization result

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) fails closed but its result is never read on this path. vacuum (api.go:33-36) checks the error correctly, so the omission is specific to dropTable. No other check exists on this path. Upstream middleware not present in file; unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error on failure, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and discards the result, so it has no effect. The only error check in the file is in vacuum (api.go:33-34), which the candidate correctly notes. No parameterization, allowlist, or path check exists before runSQL at api.go:27, which concatenates r.FormValue("t") into the SQL string. Upstream middleware is not in the file and is unverified.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: userFrom (api.go:22) unchecked assertion, dropTable (api.go:24-27) calls Authorize(u, "dba") at line 26 as a bare statement with its error discarded, and runSQL executes the concatenated DROP TABLE at line 27. An authenticated user without the dba role therefore reaches the destructive path, since the only check is ignored. Without a user in context, the assertion at api.go:22 panics before the sink, so the attacker must be authenticated, which matches the HIGH severity. The unverified upstream middleware does not change the result.

finding.claim: HIGH (dependent on AUTH-1): form parameter t is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement with no identifier validation, quoting, or parameter binding. May be downgraded to MEDIUM once AUTH-1 is fixed, if the dba role legitimately holds this capability (triage Check 7).
finding.source: Form field t via r.FormValue("t") in POST /admin/drop
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27; runSQL is an empty stub at api.go:41 so real behavior is unverified

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") read and concatenated into SQL string
runSQL stub; actual execution semantics not in file

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no identifier quoting, no parameter binding. Authorization guard bypassed by AUTH-1. Multi-statement execution unverifiable from this file.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it never blocks the request. No allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameter binding exists between r.FormValue("t") (api.go:27) and runSQL (api.go:41, empty stub). The vacuum handler at api.go:33-35 checks the error correctly, which shows the dropTable omission is the defect.
verdict.reason: Line 27 concatenates the raw form value `t` into "DROP TABLE " + t, and the only role check at api.go:26 is a discarded return value, so any authenticated user (not only dba) reaches the injection. The claim that it depends on AUTH-1 is incomplete: the discarded check is itself the bypass. Caveat: runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the multi-statement and execution behavior is not verifiable from this file, but the unsafe string construction and the missing guard are confirmed.

finding.claim: MEDIUM: admin routes /admin/drop and /admin/vacuum are served on the public all-interfaces listener with no TLS, no separate admin listener, and an ignored ListenAndServe error. Contributing factor that widens reachability of AUTH-1 and INJ-1; downgraded to MEDIUM under triage Check 5 because primary vulnerabilities exist.
finding.source: Any network host able to reach TCP port 8083
finding.sink: http.ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) exposing admin handlers registered at api.go:44-45

trace.note: ListenAndServe on ":8083" binds all interfaces; error return ignored

finding.guards_checked: No loopback binding, no internal-only listener, no host allowlist, no TLS in file. Network Reachability check (triage Check 3) finds public ingress.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check and is applied only in vacuum (api.go:33-36). dropTable calls Authorize at api.go:26 as a bare statement and discards the error, so it is not a guard. No loopback binding, host allowlist, or TLS exists between the network and the admin routes (api.go:44-46).
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: api.go:44-45 register the admin handlers and api.go:46 calls http.ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) on all interfaces with the error discarded, so any network host can reach them with no TLS and no network-level restriction. This is a hardening/exposure issue; its real impact depends on the handler-level checks, and the vacuum route's Authorize (api.go:33-36) still blocks non-dba callers. The finding should be read as a contributing factor, not a standalone exploit.

finding.claim: LOW: unchecked single-type assertion on the request context user panics per request when no user is set. Impact is a per-request panic recovered by net/http, not an outage. The string context key is also collision-prone.
finding.source: Any HTTP request to /admin/drop or /admin/vacuum without a context user set by upstream middleware
finding.sink: Type assertion .(*User) at api.go:22 panics when the value is absent or nil

trace.note: dropTable calls userFrom with no nil check
vacuum calls userFrom with no nil check

finding.guards_checked: No nil or comma-ok check in userFrom, dropTable, or vacuum. Upstream middleware not present in file.

verdict.guard_found: none. Nothing in api.go sets the "user" context value or wraps the handlers: main() (api.go:44-45) registers dropTable and vacuum directly with no middleware. The only check is the bare assertion at api.go:22, which has no comma-ok form. net/http's per-request panic recovery is not a guard against the bug, only a containment of its effect.
verdict.reason: At api.go:22, `r.Context().Value("user").(*User)` panics when the value is absent, and userFrom is called unguarded at api.go:25 and api.go:32, so any anonymous request to /admin/drop or /admin/vacuum (routed at api.go:44-45 with no middleware) panics; the candidate's trace lines are accurate. Severity is LOW as claimed, but it is a real, unauthenticated, reachable panic.
